Use case: stylized-concept. World 5 EMBER FORTRESS environment production art for a charming low-poly 2.5D platformer. Match region five of the supplied FIVE REALMS map: faceted charcoal and muted plum basalt cliffs, orange lava fissures, obsidian rocks, squat dark fortress with red banners, bronze bands and ember-lit openings. Clear broad shapes suitable for Blender low-poly modeling, crisp contours and cel-like material regions, moderate saturation. Lava is bright orange/amber with small pale-yellow core, never an all-red wash; important dark surfaces remain readable. No photoreal microtexture, no heavy smoke obscuring shapes, no extreme bloom. All objects are modelable volumes. Same coherent asset family across sheets.
Create a wide landscape full-stage concept illustration, no text/UI. Input image is style and region identity only, don't reproduce world-map layout or labels. A near-side-on 2.5D traversal with a little visible depth: left cool basalt approach with ember lanterns and broken columns, middle flat stepped basalt platforms crossing a lava chasm with a short reinforced iron bridge, right massive dark volcanic fortress on a raised plateau. Fortress has central keep, four stout battlement towers, bronze-braced portcullis, red banners with simple diamond emblem, orange-lit windows. Distant actual-volumetric scenery: cone volcano with small restrained plume, angular ridge, obsidian pillars, natural basalt arch, distant lava fall below the walk route. Foreground props: obsidian crystal cluster, cooled lava boulders, short basalt column groups, ash shrub, brazier, chained mooring post, anvil, sealed ore crate, rubble and a banner. Small ember slime and armored lava beetle for scale. A slender amber checkpoint post, rune pressure plate and open basalt exit arch near fortress. Playable surfaces mostly cooled flat grey rock, lava only in recesses and gaps, strong readable safe-route silhouettes. Stylized late-game fantasy adventure, warm rim light against neutral violet-grey daylight, not horror. No giant dragon or humanoid hero. Proposed art composition, not measured level geometry.
